newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian tax police search Fininvest group offices.
newsitem.headline: Italian tax police search Fininvest group offices.

text.p: Milan finance police searched the offices of companies in Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest media group on Tuesday as part of an inquiry into ownership of the Spanish television channel Telecinco, judicial sources said.

The searches were carried out on the order of a Milan investigating magistrate at the request of Spanish magistrates and included the foreign operations departments of Fininvest, broadcaster Mediaset and production company RTI.
A Fininvest lawyer said documents has been seized.

Former Italian prime minister Berlusconi is under investigation by anti-corruption prosecutors in Spain along with 37 other people including his brother Paolo and several Fininvest business executives.
Spanish prosecutors said last week they were investigating investments made by Fininvest in Telecinco.
They allege Fininvest had violated limits set out in Spain's private television law which says a single shareholder can only hold 25 percent in a television station.
They say Fininvest possessed more than 80 percent of Telecinco's capital and used companies, people and resident bank accounts in third countries to fake fictitious ownership.
They are also investigating alleged tax fraud of nearly two billion pesetas ($13 million) relating to investments in Telecinco.

Fininvest and Berlusconi deny they have committed crimes relating to their investments in Spain and on Tuesday Fininvest lawyer Ennio Amodio said the group was considering how to act after the searches.

"The Spanish magistrates asked for the documents relating to Fininvest's investments in Telecinco. In the request they theorise about various crimes supposedly committed against the state and the finance ministry," Amodio said.

He said he was surprised the state prosecutor's office at Milan's court of appeal had allowed the searches saying the action was against European conventions on judicial assistance between the two countries, which he said excluded intervention concerning fiscal crimes.
"We are studying whether to oppose the transfer of the seized documents but first we will try to find out exactly on what basis the Spanish judicial authorities are proceeding," Amodio said.
